{"id":"KITH-1ln3.11","title":"kith-tui: unread badge stuck after first message in a chat opened empty (fake sinceState s-0)","description":"Found in chinwag/kith-tui live smoke test 2026-10-30 (kith 556bf4c, chinwag 830be27). Demo-visible: the demo starts with empty chats.

Steps: open kith-tui with the direct chat selected and no messages in it. Type "hello from kith-tui" and press Enter. The message shows up, but the chat list keeps "bob@elsewhere.example (1)" while you're viewing it. Server state afterwards: ReadPosition {"chatId":"01M66FPR850ZG2WJBBHCZZ7V34","id":"01M66FS2JWYE0VC366HG5843CY"} with no lastReadMessageId, and Chat.unreadCount 1. For a second message in the same chat (now non-empty) the badge clears, and ReadPosition.lastReadMessageId moves forward as expected.

Cause (verified against chinwag via curl):
1. load_messages_for_chat returns LoadedMessages::default() when Message/query returns no ids (event.rs:387). That skips Message/get, so state.message_state stays "".
2. On the next Message StateChange, handle_state_change sends Message/changes with sinceState "s-0", a state chinwag never issued. RFC 8620 §5.2 says sinceState is "the current state of the client", i.e. one the server returned earlier. chinwag correctly answers ["error",{"type":"cannotCalculateChanges"}] (curl: Message/changes sinceState "s-0" -> cannotCalculateChanges; sinceState "0" -> normal response).
3. The cannotCalculateChanges branch reloads messages and returns early. It never calls mark_chat_read (that only runs at event.rs:1016 on the normal path), so the ReadPosition never advances.

Spec: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Chat unreadCount: "If lastReadMessageId is absent, all messages are counted as unread". The own-message part of this is tracked separately as chinwag-fqk0 (spec).

Fix direction: take message_state from Message/query's queryState or a Message/get with ids [] even when the chat is empty, drop the "s-0" fallback, and call mark_chat_read after the reload branch too.

new_value: Loader always issues Message/get (ids [] when empty) so message_state is a server-issued state; s-0 fallback removed (no state -> resync); resync path (no state or cannotCalculateChanges) now calls mark_chat_read.
